investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T20:34–20:41Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never left the Pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates that the two nodes eligible to run peer-pod VMs have no remaining capacity, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never starts.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other peer-pod workloads, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests. Preemption is unavailable because no lower-priority pods occupy those slots.

[Possible] The two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are present but one or both are in a NotReady, SchedulingDisabled, or cordoned state, reducing effective capacity to zero even if the resource quota appears non-zero.

[Possible] The node affinity/selector required by remote-agent pods has drifted from the actual node labels in the cluster (e.g., a node pool was replaced or relabeled), shrinking the eligible node set to only 2 nodes and making capacity exhaustion more likely.

[Less likely] A quota or LimitRange at the namespace level is capping the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations below the physical node capacity, causing the scheduler to report insufficiency even if physical slots exist.
[Less likely] A recent cluster scaling event reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a higher count, and existing workloads have not yet been rescheduled to free capacity.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-19T20:36–20:41Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested peer-pod VM because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every attempt to provision a remote agent pod times out unscheduled (~138–147 s), preventing the eval runner from reaching the agent-creation, state-polling, or runtime steps that would produce the required evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes, and preemption found no victims, meaning all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the pod requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes carry; those 2 nodes are full, so the pod is permanently unschedulable until capacity is freed or new nodes are added.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval runs: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, the eval probe will consistently lose the scheduling race.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Node-level resource leak or stuck VMs: existing peer-pod VMs may not be releasing their kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation after termination, artificially inflating consumed capacity.

If only remote-agent-state failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime passed, the failure would be localized to the state-polling logic rather than a shared scheduling constraint.

If the Unschedulable error message differed across the three sibling checks (e.g., different node counts or resource names), it would suggest independent failures rather than a single shared capacity constraint.

If a concurrent non-eval workload were found to have released its kata.peerpods.io/vm slots between the eval run and the investigation, and a re-run succeeded, it would confirm a transient capacity contention rather than a persistent exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity directly (e.g., via the Kubernetes metrics or describe API) and fails with a warning before the resource pool is fully exhausted, providing earlier signal than waiting for a pod to go Unschedulable.

Add a pre-flight scheduling check to the remote-agent eval suite that verifies at least one schedulable node exists for the remote-agent pod spec before attempting agent creation, surfacing the capacity constraint as a distinct check rather than a timeout.

Add a historical pass/fail trend eval for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime so that recurring scheduling failures can be distinguished from one-off transient events — currently verifierContext.history shows previousRunCount=0 with no baseline.

Consider a canary eval that attempts to schedule a minimal kata peer-pod on a schedule independent of the full agent lifecycle, isolating the VM scheduling layer from the agent API layer for faster triage.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 20:36 and 20:41 UTC on 2026-06-19 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both were at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence payload was returned, so the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure localized to the Kubernetes swarm cluster backing remote agent provisioning; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes (0/2 available), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner received no response evidence, causing all three remote-agents checks to time out and fail with zero evidence collected against the expected-output contract.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T20:34–20:41Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never left the Pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates that the two nodes eligible to run peer-pod VMs have no remaining capacity, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 138s before the eval timed out.

failed-check.timing: status=fail, latencyMs=140646, endedAt=2026-06-19T20:36:33.964Z — the check ran to near its warning threshold (warningLatencyMs=240000) before failing, consistent with a scheduling wait-and-timeout pattern.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, confirming the runner never reached the VM-ready state.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, matching the contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'), pod stuck 147s, no evidence collected — same root cause reproduced on a second independent probe.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'), pod stuck 145s, no evidence collected — same root cause reproduced on a third independent probe.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885 — this is the call that would submit the pod; if the pod never schedules, no VM identity is returned and evidence is never written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never starts.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other peer-pod workloads, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests. Preemption is unavailable because no lower-priority pods occupy those slots.

[Possible] The two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are present but one or both are in a NotReady, SchedulingDisabled, or cordoned state, reducing effective capacity to zero even if the resource quota appears non-zero.

[Possible] The node affinity/selector required by remote-agent pods has drifted from the actual node labels in the cluster (e.g., a node pool was replaced or relabeled), shrinking the eligible node set to only 2 nodes and making capacity exhaustion more likely.

[Less likely] A quota or LimitRange at the namespace level is capping the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations below the physical node capacity, causing the scheduler to report insufficiency even if physical slots exist.
[Less likely] A recent cluster scaling event reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a higher count, and existing workloads have not yet been rescheduled to free capacity.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-19T20:36–20:41Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested peer-pod VM because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every attempt to provision a remote agent pod times out unscheduled (~138–147 s), preventing the eval runner from reaching the agent-creation, state-polling, or runtime steps that would produce the required evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: remote-agent-state contract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none present because agent creation never completed
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes, and preemption found no victims, meaning all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the pod requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes carry; those 2 nodes are full, so the pod is permanently unschedulable until capacity is freed or new nodes are added.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval runs: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, the eval probe will consistently lose the scheduling race.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Node-level resource leak or stuck VMs: existing peer-pod VMs may not be releasing their kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation after termination, artificially inflating consumed capacity.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 20:36 and 20:41 UTC on 2026-06-19 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both were at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence payload was returned, so the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure localized to the Kubernetes swarm cluster backing remote agent provisioning; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes (0/2 available), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner received no response evidence, causing all three remote-agents checks to time out and fail with zero evidence collected against the expected-output contract.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes — concurrent eval runs, other workloads, or leaked/stuck pods from prior runs may have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for the new probe pod.

Secondary: Node affinity or selector on the remote agent pod restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, eliminating the other 4 nodes from consideration entirely, which amplifies the impact of any resource contention on those 2 nodes.
Tertiary: A prior eval run's cleanup may have failed (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs), leaving a pod or VM slot allocated and not released, reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.

Lower confidence: The cluster may have fewer kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes than required to handle concurrent remote-agent eval probes — a capacity sizing issue rather than a transient exhaustion event.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes show available (unallocated) VM slots at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint must be investigated.
If the pod's node affinity or selector was recently changed to exclude the kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, the root cause would be a misconfiguration rather than resource exhaustion.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds without any cluster changes, the failure was a transient spike in concurrent VM usage rather than a structural capacity problem.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in a subsequent run, the failure would be isolated to the runtime probe rather than a shared scheduling bottleneck.
If the eval runner's withCleanup function is confirmed to have released all pods and VM slots from prior runs, leaked resources are not the cause.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries the Kubernetes cluster for available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' status rather than a timeout failure.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote-agent pods remain in Pending or Running state after each probe cycle, catching leaked VM slot allocations before they affect subsequent runs.

Add a sibling eval that monitors the count of available kata.peerpods.io/vm resources across eligible nodes and alerts when capacity drops below the number of concurrent remote-agent eval probes configured.

Consider adding a retry-with-backoff eval variant for remote-agent-create to distinguish transient scheduling delays from persistent exhaustion, reducing false-positive outage signals from brief capacity spikes.
